# Transparency {#sec-transparency}

```{r}
#| label: setup
suppressMessages(library(here)) # for pathing to/from project directory
suppressMessages(library(tidyverse)) # for dplyr, ggplot, etc.
suppressMessages(library(janitor)) # for cleaning data
suppressMessages(library(glue)) # for cleaning data

# source scripts
clean <- readRDS(here("data", "clean.rds"))
full <- readRDS(here("data", "full.rds"))

source(here("R", "helpers.R"))
source(here("R", "plots.R"))
```

## Key takeaways

- **Materials are more often shared than data**, but still less than half the time. When items *are* made available, they're most often published directly in the article or its supplementary materials rather than deposited in a dedicated repository.
- **Raw data and analysis code are rarely made available.** The large majority of studies say nothing about whether data or code can be accessed.
- **Preregistration is essentially absent** from this literature — only a handful of studies report having preregistered their design or analysis.
- There's a visible upward trend in materials and data sharing in more recent years, likely reflecting the broader open-science movement, but it starts from a very low baseline.

## Materials availability

```{r}
#| label: fig-item-avail
#| fig-cap: "How (or whether) experimental items were made available"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

clean |> 
  mutate(item_avail = str_replace_all(item_avail, "Not Reported", "Not Provided")) |> 
  make_perc_gg_barplot("item_avail", title = "providing complete stimulus materials")
```

## Data and code availability

```{r}
#| label: fig-data-avail
#| fig-cap: "How (or whether) raw data and/or analysis code were made available"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5

clean |> 
  mutate(data_avail = str_replace_all(data_avail, "Not Reported", "Not Provided")) |> 
  make_perc_gg_barplot("data_avail", title = "providing full data or code")
```


## Changes over time

There is an encouraging increase in recent years in the provision of materials and data/code. The latter has especially gone up in the last in the last 5-10 years. But the overall proportions are still not much better than 50%.  

```{r}
#| label: fig-avail-trend
#| fig-cap: "Provision of materials has increased in recent years. Each dot represents one study with logistic smooths."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
plot_avail_by_year(clean)
```


## Preregistration

Preregistration is almost never conducted (or at least reported) in this literature. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-prereg
#| tbl-cap: "Was the study **preregistered**?"
clean |>
  count(preregistration) |>
  mutate(perc = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1),
         text = paste0(n, " (", perc, "%)")) |>
  select(preregistration, text) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = preregistration, values_from = text) |>
  rename("Preregistered" = Yes) |> 
  knitr::kable()
```
